title: Capacity: provisioned, on demand and autoscaling

videos.script: Every read and every write on DynamoDB is counted in units, and a unit is a size. {{units}} A write of one kilobyte is one write unit. A read of four kilobytes is one read unit, or half of one if it may be a moment stale. {{arithmetic}} You can pay for those units as you use them, or reserve them by the hour. Reserved is cheaper per unit, and expensive when nobody uses it. {{modes}} A short program prices a month of Quitanda's writes both ways. A steady load and a load with one busy hour come out on opposite sides. {{breakeven}} Then the autoscaling that is supposed to fix it, and why it always arrives a few minutes late. {{autoscaling}} And the limit no setting moves. One partition, and the key that sends everything to it. {{hot}} moto counts none of this, and never refuses a write. So this lesson does the arithmetic by hand, and shows where moto's numbers stop meaning anything. {{moto}}
